errorCodes.meaning: The instance's preset does not enable ATF_ENABLED.
errorCodes.remedy: raise the preset; a `prod` instance additionally needs `--ack-prod`

errorCodes.meaning: The attachment was not stored.
errorCodes.remedy: check the file size and that the target record exists

errorCodes.meaning: The instance rejected the credentials — wrong, expired, or the account is locked.
errorCodes.remedy: If a ServiceNow tool returns AUTHENTICATION_FAILED: stop immediately. Do not retry that call or make any other call to the same instance — repeated failed logins can lock the account. Tell the user to run <cli> instance test <label> and, if it fails, <cli> instance set-credentials <label>. Continue only after the user says the credentials were fixed — and then call snow_core_instances_reload before you retry, because this server still holds the credentials it read at startup and a retry without it is a second failed login

errorCodes.meaning: One or more requests in the batch failed.
errorCodes.remedy: the message lists which

errorCodes.meaning: The instance's preset does not enable CMDB_WRITE_ENABLED.
errorCodes.remedy: raise the preset; a `prod` instance additionally needs `--ack-prod`

errorCodes.meaning: The instance refused the connection and no proxy is configured.
errorCodes.remedy: `<host>` refused the connection — the instance may be hibernated (PDIs sleep after inactivity: wake it at developer.servicenow.com) or blocked by a firewall. Check the URL and its port too

errorCodes.meaning: The connection timed out with no proxy configured.
errorCodes.remedy: no answer from `<host>` in time. If this network needs a proxy, set `HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy:port` (and `NO_PROXY` for internal hosts) and run again. An idle PDI may be hibernating — wake it at developer.servicenow.com

errorCodes.meaning: The instance refused the create.
errorCodes.remedy: the message carries the instance response

errorCodes.meaning: The account lacks delete access to that table. This is not a flag.
errorCodes.remedy: use an account with the role

errorCodes.meaning: Another record references it.
errorCodes.remedy: remove the reference first

errorCodes.meaning: The instance refused the delete.
errorCodes.remedy: the message carries the instance response

errorCodes.meaning: Nothing exists at that sys_id to delete.
errorCodes.remedy: check the sys_id

errorCodes.meaning: The instance host name did not resolve (`ENOTFOUND`, `EAI_AGAIN`).
errorCodes.remedy: the name `<host>` does not resolve. Check the instance name first — a typo is the usual cause; on a corporate network the name may resolve only over VPN, or only through a proxy, so set `HTTPS_PROXY` if there is one (there is one — `<proxyVar>=<proxy>` — and a proxy does not resolve names for you unless the request goes through it, which makes a wrong name the likelier cause)

errorCodes.meaning: A refused connection surfaced with the Node identifier.
errorCodes.remedy: as `CONNECTION_REFUSED`: check the URL, the port and any proxy

errorCodes.meaning: A DNS failure surfaced with the Node identifier rather than the classified code.
errorCodes.remedy: as `DNS_FAILURE`: check the host in the store

errorCodes.meaning: The environment could not be proposed and none was given, in a run that cannot ask.
errorCodes.remedy: pass `--env pdi|dev|test|prod`. Only `devNNNNN.service-now.com` hosts are recognised as PDIs, and the environment decides the preset a write is checked against — guessing it is the one thing this wizard will not do

errorCodes.meaning: A timeout surfaced with the Node identifier.
errorCodes.remedy: as `CONNECTION_TIMEOUT`

errorCodes.meaning: A WARNING on a write that succeeded, not an error: a field the tool sent is not shown as set in the platform's response (for `snow_scr_business_rule_add`: `filter_condition` or `advanced`), or, for the ATF authoring tools, in the record read back after the write — a step input that no row attaches to the step included. The record exists without it — a Business Rule without its filter runs on every matching operation. It arrives as `warnings[].code` on the tool's result.
errorCodes.remedy: read the record back; if the field is not set, set it with a modify rather than adding the record again, and if the record is active set `active` to false first. If it is set, the response did not echo it: the column names are not documented in the bundled corpus, so check them on the instance

errorCodes.meaning: A flag that requires `WRITE_ENABLED` is on while `WRITE_ENABLED` is off. The tools gated on it are refused at run time and the refusal names WRITE first, so the entry promises a capability it cannot deliver.
errorCodes.remedy: decide which one was meant: turn WRITE on, or turn the dependent flag off. Neither is guessable from the store, so this is never repaired automatically

errorCodes.meaning: A store entry does not state all six capability flags. An absent flag is off, so the entry works — but nobody can tell an intended `false` from a forgotten one, and the next preset change starts from a guess.
errorCodes.remedy: state every flag explicitly by re-applying a preset — the review screen shows what changes before anything is written

errorCodes.meaning: The SDK ran and failed.
errorCodes.remedy: the message carries the SDK output

errorCodes.meaning: The instance's preset does not enable FLUENT_ENABLED.
errorCodes.remedy: raise the preset; a `prod` instance additionally needs `--ack-prod`

errorCodes.meaning: The ServiceNow SDK is not on `PATH`.
errorCodes.remedy: install it globally — the doctor checks `PATH`, so a checkout-local install would pass here and fail there

errorCodes.meaning: The instance is in the store but was not loaded, and the store carries the reason.
errorCodes.remedy: read the reason in the instance listing; a `prod` instance without `prodWriteAck` needs the acknowledgement

errorCodes.meaning: The instance's own rule — a data policy or a business rule — refused the record. This is not a role.
errorCodes.remedy: the instance's own rule refused the record — read the message, correct the fields it names and send the write again, as a new write with its own approval; do not change roles

errorCodes.meaning: The store entry parsed but no client could be built from it.
errorCodes.remedy: the message says which field is impossible

errorCodes.meaning: The account is authenticated but lacks a ServiceNow role for that table or operation. This is not a flag.
errorCodes.remedy: The credentials are valid but the account lacks a role for this table. Report the tool, the table and the roles the preset needs (see docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md); do not switch instances or retry with another tool to work around it

errorCodes.meaning: This checkout's own files are not the signed release's, and they could not be restored: no signed manifest is held, it does not verify, it is another release's, there is no tag to restore from, or the restore failed. Every tool is refused, as for a refused licence. A change the product could restore was restored, and is not this.
errorCodes.remedy: Run <cli> doctor: its Integrity line names the reason. <cli> licence check --refresh fetches a missing manifest; a checkout that cannot be restored is reinstalled from a signed release tag. A running Claude Code session keeps what its server read at start, so restart it afterwards

errorCodes.meaning: An argument is missing or malformed.
errorCodes.remedy: the message names the argument

errorCodes.meaning: An instance with that label is already in the store.
errorCodes.remedy: use `instance set-credentials` or `instance set-preset` to change it, `instance remove` to delete it, or `--replace` to overwrite it

errorCodes.meaning: No instance with that label is in the store this checkout resolves.
errorCodes.remedy: run `instance list` to see the labels this checkout has, or `instance add <label>` to add one

errorCodes.meaning: There is no snow-mcp 1.x store at the path the import was pointed at.
errorCodes.remedy: check the path, or pass `--path <file>` if the legacy store was kept somewhere else; `<cli> doctor` reports where it looked

errorCodes.meaning: The legacy store is not JSON this reader can parse.
errorCodes.remedy: open it and check it is a complete JSON object; a half-written file from an interrupted 1.x session cannot be migrated and its instances are re-added with `instance add`

errorCodes.meaning: This checkout's licence does not cover the call: it is missing, invalid, expired or revoked, or it is a design-only licence and the server is live. Every tool is refused, the instance-free ones included, on every build.
errorCodes.remedy: Run <cli> licence check to see why, then install a valid licence as .local/licence.json. A running Claude Code session keeps what it read at start, so restart it afterwards

errorCodes.meaning: The instance was unreachable and the cause did not match a more specific classification.
errorCodes.remedy: the message carries the underlying cause

errorCodes.meaning: The server is running and healthy; it has no instance to talk to. It stays up on purpose — an unconfigured checkout used to exit at start-up, so the moment you most needed the server to explain itself was the moment it was gone. Five tools still work: status, capabilities, reload, the instance listing and the current instance.
errorCodes.remedy: add an instance, then call the reload tool — Claude Code does not need restarting, the server re-advertises its catalogue in the same session

errorCodes.meaning: The record or table does not exist on this instance.
errorCodes.remedy: check the sys_id and the table name

errorCodes.meaning: The surface was removed.
errorCodes.remedy: the message names what replaced it

errorCodes.meaning: A Now Assist call failed.
errorCodes.remedy: the message carries the instance response; check the Now Assist licence on the instance

errorCodes.meaning: The instance's preset does not enable NOW_ASSIST_ENABLED.
errorCodes.remedy: raise the preset; a `prod` instance additionally needs `--ack-prod`

errorCodes.meaning: The OAuth client id or secret was rejected.
errorCodes.remedy: check them against the Application Registry entry on the instance

errorCodes.meaning: The instance has the OAuth password grant disabled.
errorCodes.remedy: use basic authentication, or have an administrator enable the grant type

errorCodes.meaning: The instance is tagged `environment: prod` and holds a write preset without `prodWriteAck: true`.
errorCodes.remedy: A production instance is capped at read-only. Do not suggest editing the store; the user raises it with <cli> instance set-preset <label> <preset> --ack-prod in their terminal

errorCodes.meaning: The proxy answered 407: it wants credentials before it will forward the request.
errorCodes.remedy: the proxy is asking for credentials: put them in the proxy URL (`HTTPS_PROXY=http://user:pass@proxy:port`). NTLM and Kerberos proxies are not supported — the request has to reach the instance through a proxy that accepts basic credentials

errorCodes.meaning: A proxy variable is set and nothing is listening there, or the connection to it timed out.
errorCodes.remedy: the proxy `<proxyVar>=<proxy>` did not connect to `<host>`. Check the proxy address and credentials, and that `<host>` is not excluded by `NO_PROXY` — or unset the variable if you are not behind a proxy. The proxy is printed with any credentials masked

errorCodes.meaning: The instance refused the query.
errorCodes.remedy: the message carries the instance response

errorCodes.meaning: The instance is throttling this account.
errorCodes.remedy: retry later; reduce `maxRecords` or the call rate

errorCodes.meaning: The request failed and the instance response is the only information there is.
errorCodes.remedy: the message carries that response

errorCodes.meaning: A tool needed a table schema that has not been read this session.
errorCodes.remedy: call the schema read tool for that table first

errorCodes.meaning: The script ran and errored.
errorCodes.remedy: the message carries the instance output

errorCodes.meaning: The instance's preset does not enable SCRIPTING_ENABLED.
errorCodes.remedy: raise the preset; a `prod` instance additionally needs `--ack-prod`

errorCodes.meaning: this checkout is under <provider> (<root>). File mode 0600 does not stop synchronisation — the credential store would be uploaded to that service.
errorCodes.remedy: move the checkout outside the synced folder, or keep credentials in the global store with `--global` (<global> is not synced by default)

errorCodes.meaning: `SNOW_STORE` names a file that is not there — an explicit override is never a fallback.
errorCodes.remedy: correct the variable, unset it, or create the store

errorCodes.meaning: The store holds a password and is group/world-readable, or sits in a group/world-writable directory (D-04).
errorCodes.remedy: tighten the mode; on Windows the check is skipped and the doctor notes it instead

errorCodes.meaning: The store parsed but a field is wrong; the message names its path, for example `instances.pdi.flags.WRITE_ENABLED`.
errorCodes.remedy: the message names the field path; correct it in the store

errorCodes.meaning: The store was written by a NEWER server than this one — a checkout left behind, not a broken file.
errorCodes.remedy: upgrade this checkout, rather than editing the store down; a backup can be restored if the newer server wrote one

errorCodes.meaning: The store was written by an older server and this build does not read that schema. Nothing migrates on load — an explicit command is what rewrites a credential file.
errorCodes.remedy: migrate it; a 0600 backup is written first and credential values are never touched

errorCodes.meaning: The store exists but is not valid JSON.
errorCodes.remedy: repair or recreate it; the message names the parse error

errorCodes.meaning: The certificate was not signed by a CA this machine trusts — normal on a network that intercepts TLS.
errorCodes.remedy: the certificate presented for `<host>` is not trusted by Node (issuer: `<issuer>`) — typically a TLS-intercepting gateway, or an expired certificate. Export the gateway root CA as PEM, point `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` at it for the shell that runs <cli> and in `.claude/settings.local.json` → `env` so the server gets it too, and restart — Node reads it once, at process start. Never `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0`: it disables verification for the whole process, which on an intercepting network means trusting the interceptor and every other certificate with it

errorCodes.meaning: The certificate is invalid for reasons other than an untrusted root — expired, or the wrong host.
errorCodes.remedy: check the instance URL and the certificate; this is not a CA-trust problem

errorCodes.meaning: Server defect: a tool declares a gate the evaluator does not know.
errorCodes.remedy: report it; no user action can help

errorCodes.meaning: No instance in the store carries that label.
errorCodes.remedy: the listing prints the labels that exist

errorCodes.meaning: A retired or misspelled tool name.
errorCodes.remedy: use the `snow_*` name from `governance/mcp-protocols.md`; maintainers: `npm run lint:contract`

errorCodes.meaning: The tool is registered, the preset let it through, and the server refused without contacting the instance: the operation has no REST endpoint on any instance. The two script-execution stubs stay registered because removing the names would turn a clear refusal into UNKNOWN_TOOL, which reads as "you spelled it wrong" and sends you hunting a typo that is not there. They fail before any HTTP request, so nothing reaches the instance and nothing is half-done.
errorCodes.remedy: take the other route: run the script in System Definition > Scripts - Background, or author a Fix Script and run it from the UI. Keep `sys_script_fix.name` to 40 characters — the platform truncates it over REST without an error (see `docs/PLATFORM-NOTES.md` PN-07); a write through this server returns a `VALUE_TRUNCATED` warning

errorCodes.meaning: The instance refused the update.
errorCodes.remedy: the message carries the instance response

errorCodes.meaning: The URL embeds a user name or password, which would put a secret in the store URL and in logs.
errorCodes.remedy: remove them; the wizard asks for credentials separately

errorCodes.meaning: The URL carries a path; only the origin is stored.
errorCodes.remedy: drop everything after the host

errorCodes.meaning: The value is not a URL the server can parse.
errorCodes.remedy: enter it as `https://<host>.service-now.com`

errorCodes.meaning: The URL is not https. Credentials would cross the network in clear.
errorCodes.remedy: use the https form of the same host

errorCodes.meaning: The wizard needs an instance URL and none was given.
errorCodes.remedy: enter the full https URL of the instance; non-interactively pass `--url <origin>` (a URL cannot be proposed)

errorCodes.meaning: An argument is present but not the expected shape.
errorCodes.remedy: the message names the argument and the shape

errorCodes.meaning: A WARNING on a write that succeeded, not an error: a field the tool sent reads back with a different value — neither missing nor a cut prefix — once line endings are normalised (the ATF authoring tools, ARC-09-C95). It names the field, the first differing offset and both lengths, never the values. Also raised when more than one row holds a step input that should be held once.
errorCodes.remedy: the record exists with the stored value: read it back and, if that value is wrong, correct it with a modify — do not add it again, which would make a second record

errorCodes.meaning: A write refused BEFORE it was sent (ARC-09-C97): a string is longer than its column's `max_length`, read fresh from `sys_dictionary` for this write — on the table that defines the column, which for an inherited one is a table it extends. Nothing was written by this write. Lengths are counted in code points, as VALUE_TRUNCATED counts them. When the same call wrote other records first, the error lists them (`details.written`).
errorCodes.remedy: shorten the value to at most the stated length and send the write again; records the call already wrote (named in the error) exist, so do not add them again

errorCodes.meaning: A WARNING on a write that succeeded, not an error: a string appears to have been cut at its column — the platform stored only the first part of it, without refusing. It arrives as `warnings[].code` on the tool's result (or as a note on the error of a tool that failed after it wrote) and names the field, both lengths and a limit. The limit is the dictionary's stated `max_length` when `confirmed` is true, and otherwise the stored length, which is a lower bound; a column defined on a parent table never confirms.
errorCodes.remedy: the record exists with the stored value, so modify it with a value of at most `column_limit` characters (when `confirmed` is false that length is only known to fit); do not add it again, which would make a second record. If the record is active, set `active` to false until it is corrected

errorCodes.meaning: The instance's preset does not enable WRITE_ENABLED.
errorCodes.remedy: raise the preset; a `prod` instance additionally needs `--ack-prod`
